title: Local Kubo--Mori weighting of the fractional shell with arbitrary prefixes
question: Can a local Gibbs Kubo--Mori/Dirichlet weight suppress the cutoff growth of the theta=1/2 fractional shell while every split prefix is retained?
method: Diagonalize the doubled actual-Q3 bond generator and construct normalized local Gibbs probabilities at beta 1/2 and 1.
Evaluate the logarithmic-mean Kubo--Mori weights with the exact diagonal limit and compare them with the arithmetic mean.
Retain every prefix position in forward and reverse split orders for V=2 d=3..6 and V=4 d=2, with both signs, adjoints, sites and betas.
Check the weighted spectral phase identity and theta=1/2 finite-time bound in primary and non-importing independent lanes, then compare them in the integrated verifier and compile Lean R368.
finding: Primary and independent lanes each pass 4636/4636 assertions over 656 contexts; integrated passes 65/65 and Lean R368 passes. The maximum Kubo--Mori weighted fractional norm is 1.208758407679001 with bound 0.4029194692263337 and change-to-bound ratio 0.3868613066541026, while the corresponding R-367 unweighted maximum is 69.90869910391245. The largest arithmetic-to-Kubo fractional ratio is 1.7169449837129835 and the primary-independent numeric difference is 1.7053025658242404e-13.
decision_reason: The local Kubo--Mori weight materially suppresses the finite high-frequency shell relative to the unweighted R-367 diagnostic and remains valid over every finite split prefix. This identifies a sharper QFT-facing topology candidate, but the weight is only a doubled local bond Gibbs proxy; no cutoff/volume/source/history/shape-uniform comparison or global KMS transfer is established.

adversarial_review.check: The Gibbs probabilities come from the doubled local bond generator and are explicitly not identified with the full interacting KMS state.
Equal log-probability gaps use the arithmetic-limit value; both lanes check finite positivity and symmetry.
Every position from zero through full is evaluated in both split orientations; no intermediate prefix is omitted.
The finite d=3..6 and V=4,d=2 table is not a regulator-uniform or infinite-volume theorem.
The actual matrix phase coefficients are compared directly with the doubled unitary and the scalar envelope is compiled in Lean R368.
Common core, common alpha, OS/KMS/GNS dynamics, gap, continuum, C6, Sector-A and Pre-A remain open.

next_action: Derive an analytic local Kubo--Mori/Dirichlet comparison with cutoff-independent weights and test source translations and exhaustion shapes; register any rigorous lower-growth obstruction separately.
boundary: T0 claim-nonbearing finite local weighted-topology diagnostic only. The doubled bond Gibbs weight is not a global KMS state, and common core, common alpha, OS/KMS/GNS dynamics, mass gap, continuum, C6, Sector-A and Pre-A remain open.
no_overclaim: R-368 records finite weighted suppression and complete prefix coverage; it does not prove regulator uniformity or a QFT theorem.
